answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the haven schedule in the basalt ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the harbor checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 175 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 23 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
